title: Low-Cal Smoky Tomato Soup
subtitle: with Haloumi Croutons and Crusty Rolls
description: Think eating light means eating boring? Not in our book! Our low-cal recipes have all the punchy flavour and excitement you’d expect from us, and just 450 to 599 calories per serve.

steps.text: Grill capsicum: Preheat the grill to high. Line an oven tray with foil. Quarter the capsicum and put on the lined tray, skin side up. Grill for 10-12 mins until the skin is slightly blackened. Cover and stand for 5 mins to allow the skin to steam and loosen. Remove the skin (see Kitchen hack). Reserve the lined tray and keep the grill on high.

Prep ingredients: While the capsicum is grilling, coarsely chop the onion. Coarsely chop the parsley leaves and finely chop the stems, keeping them separate. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Cut the haloumi into 3cm chunks.

Soften onion: Heat 1 tsp olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, for 3-4 mins until softened. Add the capsicum, parsley stems, barbecue seasoning, half the tomato paste, 60ml (¼ cup) milk and 2 tsp sugar and stir to combine. Remove the pan from the heat.

Simmer soup: Blend the capsicum mixture with a stick blender or food processor until smooth. Return the pan to high heat, add the tomatoes and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 5 mins or until slightly thickened. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Serve up: Meanwhile, combine the garlic and 1 tbs olive oil in a large bowl. Add the haloumi and toss to coat. Put the haloumi and bread rolls on the reserved tray and grill for 4-5 mins until golden brown. Divide the soup among bowls. Top with the haloumi and scatter over the remaining parsley. Serve with the bread rolls and enjoy!

Kitchen hack: We're going to blend the capsicum mixture in Step 4 with a stick blender or food processor. If you don't have one, no worries! After peeling the capsicum, cut it into 2cm chunks. Then, simply skip the blending step and continue with the recipe to make a chunky, rustic-style soup.
